P.G. was partially supported by Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico (CNPq) and by Coordenaçã
arxiv-2202-03128.creator: Gabriela Estevez, Pablo Guarino
arxiv-2202-03128.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Gabriela Estevez, Pablo Guarino. A general ansatz in Renormalization Theory, already established in many important situations, states that exponential convergence of renormalization orbits implies that topological conjugacies are actually smooth (when restricted to the attractors of the original systems). In this paper we establish this principle for a large class of bicritical circle maps , which are C 3 C^{3} circle homeomorphisms with irrational rotation number and exactly two (non-flat) critical points.

arxiv-2202-04907.title: Efficient Generation of Spin Cat States
arxiv-2202-04907.creator: Jiahao Huang, Hongtao Huo, Min Zhuang, Chaohong Lee
arxiv-2202-04907.description: Abstract Spin cat states are promising candidates for achieving Heisenberg-limited quantum metrology. It is suggested that spin cat states can be generated by adiabatic evolution. However, due to the limited coherence time, the adiabatic process may be too slow to be practical. To speed up the state generation, we propose to use machine optimization to generate desired spin cat states.

arxiv-2304-04276.title: Portability and Scalability of OpenMP Offloading on State-of-the-art Accelerators
arxiv-2304-04276.creator: Yehonatan Fridman, Guy Tamir, Gal Oren
arxiv-2304-04276.description: Abstract Over the last decade, most of the increase in computing power has been gained by advances in accelerated many-core architectures, mainly in the form of GPGPUs. While accelerators achieve phenomenal performances in various computing tasks, their utilization requires code adaptations and transformations.

arxiv-2305-14917.title: Structural Ambiguity and its Disambiguation in Language Model Based Parsers: the Case of Dutch Clause Relativization
arxiv-2305-14917.creator: Gijs Wijnholds, Michael Moortgat
arxiv-2305-14917.description: Abstract This paper addresses structural ambiguity in Dutch relative clauses. By investigating the task of disambiguation by grounding , we study how the presence of a prior sentence can resolve relative clause ambiguities. We apply this method to two parsing architectures in an attempt to demystify the parsing and language model components of two present-day neural parsers.

arxiv-2310-03186.title: Inferring Inference
arxiv-2310-03186.creator: Rajkumar Vasudeva Raju, Zhe Li, Scott Linderman, Xaq Pitkow
arxiv-2310-03186.description: Abstract Patterns of microcircuitry in the cerebral cortex suggest that the brain has an array of repeated elementary or “canonical” computational units. However, neural representations are distributed, so the relevant computations may only be related indirectly to single-neuron transformations. It thus remains an open challenge how to define canonical distributed computations.

arxiv-2510-00916.title: New variants of N = 3 , 4 N=3,4 superconformal mechanics
arxiv-2510-00916.description: Abstract We construct superconformal mechanics with N = 3 N=3 and N = 4 N=4 supersymmetries that were inspired by analogies with the supersymmetric Schwarzian mechanics. The Schwarzian, being another system with superconformal symmetry, provides insight into the field content of supersymmetric mechanics, most notably, on the number and properties of the fermionic fields involved.

pmc-10617927.title: A potential protective role of congenital peritoneal encapsulation coexisting with metastatic colon cancer: a rare case report
pmc-10617927.creator: Youssef Ahmad, Joud Fahed, Jebrail Mousa, Fadi Souleiman
pmc-10617927.description: Introduction and importance:Congenital peritoneal encapsulation (CPE) is a rare condition in which the small intestine is encased within a mesothelial-lined sac. The following case is an extremely rare description of the co-existence of both colon cancer and peritoneal encapsulation, highlighting the potential role of this co-existence in preventing the spread of metastases and tumor implantation.

pmc-11334456.title: Medication non-adherence and associated factors among peoples with schizophrenia: multicenter cross-sectional study in Northwest Ethiopia
pmc-11334456.creator: Fasil Bayafers Tamene, Endalamaw Aschale Mihiretie, Abiy Mulugeta, Abenet Kassaye, Kale Gubae, Samuel Agegnew Wondm
pmc-11334456.description: BackgroundSchizophrenia is a serious and debilitating psychiatric disorder that is linked to marked social and occupational impairment. Despite the vital relevance of medication, non-adherence with recommended pharmacological treatments has been identified as a worldwide problem and is perhaps the most difficult component of treating schizophrenia.

pmc-11419311.title: Venous thromboembolism after aesthetic surgeries in low-risk patients without hypercoagulability
pmc-11419311.creator: René M Palacios Huatuco, Gabriel Giovanardi, Alejandro Coloccini, Mariano F Ramírez, Hernán F Sala, Horacio F Mayer
pmc-11419311.description: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a serious but rare complication of aesthetic surgery, with an incidence of 0.017% for liposuction and 0.01%–0.02% for augmentation mammoplasty. Despite the low incidence and appropriate patient selection, we present two cases of VTE in low-risk patients without hypercoagulability undergoing aesthetic procedures.

pmc-11626360.title: Investigating metabolic syndrome markers and body mass index changes in patients with acne vulgaris treated with isotretinoin: A prospective study
pmc-11626360.creator: Afsaneh Sadeghzadeh Bazargan, Alireza Jafarzadeh, Fatemeh Danandeh, Sepideh Salehi
pmc-11626360.description: BackgroundAcne vulgaris is a common inflammatory skin disease that occurs during puberty, affecting approximately 85% of young adults and may persist into adulthood. The pathophysiology of acne is multifactorial, involving hormonal, inflammatory, and immune mechanisms. Isotretinoin is widely used for treating severe cystic acne or recurrent acne.

pmc-12508182.title: Development and validation of an age estimation model based on dental characteristics using panoramic radiographs
pmc-12508182.creator: Sehyun Oh, Jaehan Park, Byung-Yoon Roh, Akiko Kumagai, Sang-Seob Lee
pmc-12508182.description: Dental characteristics have considerable potential as indicators for estimating chronological age. This study developed a regression model for age estimation using dental characteristics observed in panoramic radiographs. A total of 2,391 radiographs from individuals aged 20 to 89 years were analyzed, with a focus on five treatment-induced characteristics.

pmc-13047673.title: La3+ Networks and Speciation in the Molten State: Impact of Spacer Salt Selection on Structural Heterogeneity
pmc-13047673.creator: Bichitra Borah, Matthew S. Emerson, Santanu Roy, John J. Ferrari, Karena W. Chapman, Leighanne C. Gallington, Diwash Dhakal, Ellie M. Kim, Phillip W. Halstenberg, Sheng Dai, Simerjeet K. Gill, James F. Wishart, Claudio J. Margulis
pmc-13047673.description: We recently introduced the concept of a “spacer salt” that creates structural heterogeneity and intermediate range order. Put simply, a fully networked salt melt, such as LaCl3 or UCl3, becomes disrupted by the introduction of ions that do not participate in the network.

pmc-13049019.title: The emergence of trust under conditions of distrust
pmc-13049019.creator: Anna Lena Fehlhaber
pmc-13049019.description: The genesis of trust between strangers on the Internet - without the protective and structuring framework of digital platforms - is a topic that has been little researched so far. This need for research is exploratively approached via an experimental social deduction game, which is intended to make online trust decisions visible under distrustful conditions.

pmc-13471658.title: Automated insulin delivery in type 2 diabetes: a meta-analysis of randomized trials protocol
pmc-13471658.creator: Luis Gordillo-Rosas, Cindy Lee Cajachagua-Pucuhuaranga, Julián Santa Cruz-Venegas, Luis Mateus Urrutia-Osorio, Samir Pantoja, Jimena Lozano-Núñez, Oriana Rivera-Lozada, Cesar Bonilla-Asalde, Joshuan J. Barboza
pmc-13471658.description: BackgroundType 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a highly prevalent chronic metabolic disorder, and a substantial proportion of patients eventually require insulin therapy, which is frequently complicated by therapeutic inertia, hypoglycemia and glycemic variability. Automated insulin delivery (AID) systems combine continuous glucose monitoring with algorithm-driven insulin delivery, but their efficacy and safety in adults with T2DM remain uncertain.
